sources.label: Destination NSW - Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk
Randwick City Council - Beaches and coast

blocks.text: If you only have time for one stretch of Sydney coastline, make it the Eastern Suburbs beaches - Bondi, Tamarama, Bronte, Clovelly, Gordons Bay, Coogee and Maroubra, strung along about six kilometres of headland. I've walked this coast in every mood, and the short version I give friends is: Bondi for the buzz, Bronte for a swim with the kids, Clovelly and Gordons Bay for snorkelling, Coogee to finish with a beer. Here's how I'd actually spend the day.

items.label: How I get around
items.value: The clifftop coastal walk on foot

blocks.text: Start at Bondi - the famous one, for good reason

Bondi is the beach that ends up on the postcards, and I never tire of it - a wide sweep of pale sand with a flagged swimming area, a busy café promenade and a sea pool at each end. The Icebergs pool at the southern tip is the iconic one; swimming a few laps there with waves crashing over the wall is a rite of passage. Sessions and lane availability change seasonally, so check the Icebergs website before you go rather than trusting a timetable I might have out of date.
Bondi's parking is a headache on any warm weekend. I'll often park near Coogee or take the bus, walk north to Bondi, then stroll back - you get the whole coast twice and never circle a car park.
The walk south: Tamarama, Bronte and the sea baths

From Bondi's southern end the coastal walk begins - my favourite way to see the lot. First up is Tamarama - locals call it 'Glamarama' - a small, pretty pocket beach hemmed by cliffs. It's beautiful, but the surf can be powerful and the rips serious: swim only between the flags when it's patrolled, and if in doubt, just press on.

A little further on is Bronte, which might be the most complete beach on the coast for a family day: a patrolled surf beach, a grassy park with barbecues and shade, a kiosk row, and the Bronte Baths carved into the rocks for a sheltered swim when the shore break is dumping. It's the classic midpoint of the walk.

blocks.title: Read the beach before you swim
blocks.text: Conditions on this coast change fast - Tamarama, Bronte and Maroubra can all throw strong rips. Always swim between the red-and-yellow flags at a patrolled beach, and check the daily surf report on the Beachsafe app (Surf Life Saving Australia) before you get in.
The snorkelling middle: Clovelly and Gordons Bay

This is the part visitors often miss, and I'd send you here first. Clovelly isn't a wide sandy beach at all - it's a long, narrow bay between two rock shelves, with flat concrete edges to lay a towel on and steps into calm, clear water. Because it's so sheltered it's brilliant for kids learning to snorkel, with plenty to see from little fish to the resident blue gropers. Around the headland, Gordons Bay is a quiet cobbled cove with a marked underwater nature trail for snorkellers and divers. Both sit inside the Bronte–Coogee Aquatic Reserve, so it's look-don't-touch - no fishing or collecting.
Finish at Coogee (with Maroubra as a bonus)

Coogee is where I like to end up: a friendly, family-sized beach with a Norfolk-pine promenade made for an evening walk and pubs and cafés a block back for a well-earned feed. It's also home to a cluster of ocean pools - Wylie's Baths on the southern headland, and McIver's Baths, a historic women-and-children's swimming spot. Entry fees and hours for the tidal pools change, so check locally on the day. If you've still got legs, Maroubra sits further south - a long, surf-serious beach that's less crowded, with a skate park and playground.

items.q: What's the best order to visit the Eastern Suburbs beaches?
items.a: I walk north-to-south: Bondi, Tamarama, Bronte, Clovelly, Gordons Bay, then Coogee, with Maroubra as an optional extra beyond. Finishing at Coogee means plenty of pubs and cafés for a late lunch or sunset drink.

items.q: How long is the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk?
items.a: It's roughly six kilometres one way and most people take about two hours at a relaxed pace, longer with swims and coffee stops. It's a sealed clifftop path with some stairs - just bring water, sun protection and decent shoes.

items.q: Which beach is best for snorkelling?
items.a: Clovelly and Gordons Bay. Clovelly's sheltered channel is calm and easy for kids, while Gordons Bay has a marked underwater nature trail. Both sit inside the Bronte–Coogee Aquatic Reserve, so it's look-but-don't-take.
Bronte and Clovelly are my picks - Bronte has a grassy park, barbecues and the sheltered Bronte Baths, and Clovelly's calm water is ideal for little swimmers. Coogee is gentle too.

items.q: Do I need to pay or book anything?
items.a: The beaches and the coastal walk are free. Some ocean pools charge a small entry fee and hours vary seasonally, so check on the day. Parking is the real cost on warm weekends - buses or an early start save the stress.

blocks.text: That's the whole coast in a day: Bondi's energy, the cliff path through Bronte's parkland, the clear water at Clovelly and Gordons Bay, and Coogee as the light goes gold. Bring a towel, sunscreen and time to spare - it's the stretch of Sydney I never tire of showing people.
